items.title: Section: Supreme Equanimity — the First Benefit of Realising Phenomena's Selflessness

items.zh: 如是菩薩行勝義故，於一切法平等平等。以真如慧如實觀察，於一切處具平等見、具平等心，得最勝捨。
items.en: Such a bodhisattva, by practising in accordance with ultimate meaning, regards every phenomenon as utterly equal. Observing truly with the wisdom of suchness, they possess an equal view and an equal mind towards every sense-field, and thereby attain supreme equanimity.

items.zh: 依止此捨，於諸明處一切善巧勤修習時，雖復遭遇一切劬勞、一切苦難，而不退轉，速疾能令身無勞倦、心無勞倦。

items.title: Mastery of the Five Fields, Achieved Without Pride, and Faced Without Fear

items.zh: 於諸善巧速能成辦，得大念力。不因善巧而自貢高，亦於他所無有祕吝。
items.en: They quickly master these various skills, gaining great mindful power. Yet they do not become conceited because of this skill, nor are they secretive or stingy with it towards others.

items.zh: 於諸善巧心無怯弱，有所堪能。所行無礙，具足堅固甲冑加行。
items.en: Towards these various skills their mind holds no timidity, and they possess genuine capability. Whatever they undertake proceeds without obstruction, equipped with the firm, armour-like exertion that never wavers.

items.title: Section: Samsara Never Wasted — Four Paradoxical Marks of Genuine Progress

items.zh: 是諸菩薩於生死中，如如流轉遭大苦難，如是如是於其無上正等菩提堪能增長。如如獲得尊貴殊勝，如是如是於諸有情憍慢漸減。
items.en: The more these bodhisattvas, in the midst of birth-and-death, encounter great suffering and hardship as they cycle onward, the more they become capable of increasing their unsurpassed, perfect awakening. And the more distinguished honour and prestige they attain, the more their pride towards other beings correspondingly diminishes.

items.zh: 如如證得智慧殊勝，如是如是倍於他所難詰、諍訟、諠雜語論、本惑、隨惑、犯禁現行，能數觀察深心棄捨。如如功德展轉增長，如是如是轉覆自善、不求他知、亦不希求利養恭敬。
items.en: The more distinguished wisdom they realise, the more they repeatedly observe, and deeply abandon any inclination towards, others' hostile questioning, disputation, noisy quarrelsome talk, the manifestation of root afflictions, secondary afflictions, or precept violations. And the more their virtuous qualities progressively increase, the more they conceal their own goodness, neither seeking that others know of it, nor desiring gain or reverence.

items.title: Section: Every Benefit Just Described Rests on a Single Wisdom, Unsurpassed and Unrivaled

items.zh: 如是等類菩薩所有眾多勝利是菩提分。隨順菩提，皆依彼智。
items.en: All such benefits belonging to bodhisattvas as these are factors of awakening. Whatever accords with awakening depends entirely on that same wisdom.

items.zh: 是故一切已得菩提、當得、今得，皆依彼智。除此更無若劣若勝。
items.en: Therefore, all who have attained awakening in the past, will attain it in the future, or are attaining it now depend entirely on that same wisdom. Apart from this, there is nothing else, whether lesser or greater, that could serve the same role.

items.title: Section: Practice Free of Conceptual Proliferation — The Foundation for the Six Perfections

items.zh: 又諸菩薩乘御如是無戲論理，獲得如是眾多勝利。
items.en: Moreover, riding upon this very theory free of conceptual proliferation, bodhisattvas obtain all these many benefits just described.

items.zh: 為自成熟諸佛法故，為成熟他三乘法故，修行正行。
items.en: In order to mature the buddha-dharmas within themselves, and in order to mature the teachings of the three vehicles in others, they carry out genuine practice.

items.title: Giving, Precepts, and Patience as Practice Free of Conceptual Proliferation

items.zh: 彼於如是修正行時，於自身財遠離貪愛，於諸眾生學離貪愛，能捨身財，唯為利益諸眾生故。
items.en: As they carry out this genuine practice, they remain free of attachment to their own body and wealth, and train other beings to become free of such attachment as well — able to give up body and wealth solely for the benefit of all beings.

items.zh: 又能防護、極善防護由身語等修學律儀，性不樂惡，性極賢善。又能忍他一切侵惱，於行惡者能學堪忍，性薄瞋忿，不侵惱他。
items.en: They are also able to guard, and most excellently guard, the moral discipline they train in through body, speech, and mind, being by nature disinclined towards wrongdoing and by nature deeply virtuous. They are further able to bear every manner of harm and disturbance from others, learning to remain patient even towards those who act wrongly — their anger and resentment naturally thin, so that they never disturb or harm others in turn.

items.title: Diligence's Threefold Purpose Across the Five Fields of Knowledge

items.zh: 又能勤修一切明處令其善巧，為斷眾生一切疑難，為惠眾生諸饒益事，為自攝受一切智因。
items.en: They are also able to diligently cultivate every field of knowledge until skilled in it, in order to resolve every doubt and difficulty of sentient beings, in order to bestow every kind of genuine benefit upon sentient beings, and in order to gather within themselves the cause of omniscience.

items.title: Concentration — Stabilising the Mind to Purify the Four Immeasurables and Unlock the Five Superknowledges

items.zh: 又能於內安住其心令心善定，於心安住常勤修學，為淨修治四種梵住，為能遊戲五種神通，為能成立利眾生事，為欲除遣精勤修學一切善巧所生勞倦。
items.en: They are also able to settle the mind internally so that it becomes well concentrated, diligently training so that this settled state is constantly maintained — in order to purify and cultivate the four divine abidings, in order to freely exercise the five superknowledges, in order to accomplish what genuinely benefits sentient beings, and in order to dispel the very fatigue produced by diligently mastering every skill.

items.title: Wisdom Completes the Six Perfections, Defined Through the Seven Marks of Genuine Greatness

items.zh: 又性黠慧成極真智，為極真智常勤修學，為自當來般涅槃故修習大乘。
items.en: They are also, by nature, sharply intelligent, and this matures into genuinely transcendent wisdom; they diligently train so that this transcendent wisdom continually deepens; and, for the sake of their own future final nirvāṇa, they cultivate the Great Vehicle.

items.zh: 又諸菩薩即於如是修正行時，

items.title: Section: Benefiting Beings — Four Ways a Bodhisattva Treats the Virtuous, the Flawed, the Hostile, and the Indebting

items.zh: 於具功德諸有情所，常樂現前供養恭敬。於具過失諸有情所，常樂現前發起最勝悲心、愍心，隨能隨力，令彼除斷所有過失。
items.en: Towards sentient beings possessing genuine virtue, they constantly delight in offering reverence and respect in person. Towards sentient beings possessing faults, they constantly delight in generating the most excellent compassion and sympathy towards them, helping them, to whatever extent their ability allows, to cut off every one of their faults.

items.zh: 於己有怨諸有情所，常起慈心，隨能隨力，無諂無誑，作彼種種利益安樂，令彼怨者意樂加行所有過失及怨嫌心自然除斷。於己有恩諸有情所，善知恩故，若等若增現前酬報，隨能隨力，如法令其意望滿足。雖無力能，彼若求請，即於彼彼所作事業示現殷重精勤營務，終不頓止彼所希求，
items.en: Towards sentient beings who hold hostility against them, they constantly generate loving-kindness, and, to whatever extent their ability allows, without flattery and without deception, perform every kind of act that genuinely benefits and brings ease — so that the hostile being's own faults of intention and action, and their very hostility, dissolve of their own accord. Towards sentient beings to whom they owe gratitude, knowing that debt well, they repay it in the present with equal or greater generosity, to whatever extent their ability allows, satisfying that being's hopes in a fitting way. And even lacking the actual ability, if such a being makes a request, they show earnest, diligent effort towards whatever task is asked, never abruptly refusing what is sought.

items.zh: 云何令彼知我無力，非無欲樂。

items.title: Section: Entering the Inexpressible Nature of Phenomena — What Reasoning Alone Can Establish

items.zh: 如是等類，當知名為菩薩乘御無戲論理，依極真智修正加行。
items.en: All such practices as these should be understood as a bodhisattva riding upon the theory free of conceptual proliferation, cultivating genuine practice on the basis of transcendent wisdom.

items.zh: 以何道理應知諸法離言自性？
items.en: By what reasoning should it be understood that phenomena possess an inexpressible nature?

items.title: Section: Why a Name Never Reaches Its Object — The Yogācāra Account of Speech and Mental Image

items.zh: 謂一切法假立自相，或說為色，或說為受，如前廣說乃至涅槃。當知一切唯假建立，非有自性。亦非離彼別有自性，是言所行、是言境界。
items.en: All phenomena possess only an imputed characteristic — spoken of as form, as feeling, and so on as elaborated before, all the way up to nirvāṇa. It should be understood that all of this is established merely through imputation, and does not possess a nature of its own. Nor, apart from that imputation, is there some separate nature which is the object of speech's own activity, the sphere in which speech operates.

items.title: Section: Ultimate Existence — Neither Superimposing a Fixed Nature Nor Denying the Dependent Nature Itself

items.zh: 如是諸法，非有自性如言所說，亦非一切都無所有。如是非有，亦非一切都無所有。云何而有？
items.en: Phenomena of this kind do not possess a nature exactly as language describes them, yet neither are they utterly nonexistent in every sense ... in what way, then, do they exist?

items.zh: 謂離增益實無妄執，及離損減實有妄執，如是而有；即是諸法勝義自性。當知唯是無分別智所行境界。
items.en: Departing from the false clinging of superimposition, which adds a reality that genuinely is not there, and departing from the false clinging of denial, which subtracts a reality that genuinely is there — existing in just this way is precisely phenomena's ultimate own-nature. This should be understood as the object experienced only by non-discriminating wisdom.

blocks.text: What insight into the selflessness of phenomena makes possible in practice, and then the beginning of the argument that phenomena are "inexpressible".
"Regarding every phenomenon as equal, observing with the wisdom of suchness", one has "an equal view and an equal mind towards every sense-field".
One masters the fields of knowledge quickly, "yet does not become conceited, nor secretive or stingy with it towards others".

"The more they encounter suffering in saṃsāra, the more their awakening increases. The more honour they gain, the more their pride decreases." "The more their virtues increase, the more they conceal their own good qualities." Venerable Miào Jìng comments.

"Riding upon this theory free of conceptual proliferation", bodhisattvas practise the six perfections: giving up body and wealth for beings; guarding discipline; bearing harm; mastering every field of knowledge "to resolve every doubt of beings"; settling the mind "to purify the four divine abidings and exercise the superknowledges"; and cultivating transcendent wisdom.
Towards the virtuous, reverence; towards those with faults, compassion; towards the hostile, loving-kindness, "without flattery or deception"; towards those who have helped them, gratitude repaid.

"All phenomena possess only an imputed characteristic, spoken of as form, feeling, up to nirvāṇa", "established merely through imputation", without a nature of their own. "Yet neither are they utterly nonexistent." They exist "departing from superimposition, which adds a reality not there, and from denial, which subtracts a reality that is there".

quiz.q: "Attaining supreme equanimity" — how do the masters explain?
options: Miào Jìng: attachment is sticking, equanimity not sticking; Cháng Bǎi: worldly meditative equanimity without suchness-wisdom isn't "supreme"
quiz.why: "Observing truly with the wisdom of suchness, they possess an equal view and an equal mind towards every sense-field, and thereby attain supreme equanimity." Venerable Miào Jìng: attachment is sticking; equanimity is not sticking. Master Cháng Bǎi: the equanimous feeling of worldly dhyāna, without suchness-wisdom, is an ordinary state — not supreme equanimity.

quiz.q: "Not conceited, nor secretive or stingy with others." How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain the latter?
options: towards those learning from the bodhisattva — not stingy or secretive, but teaching them
quiz.why: "Yet they do not become conceited because of this skill, nor are they secretive or stingy with it towards others." Master Cháng Bǎi: towards others learning from the bodhisattva, he won't be stingy or secretive and withhold teaching.

quiz.q: "The more (如如) they encounter hardship, the more awakening grows." How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain 如如?
options: describes the countless kinds of hardship the bodhisattva meets
quiz.why: "The more these bodhisattvas, in the midst of birth-and-death, encounter great suffering and hardship as they cycle onward, the more they become capable of increasing their unsurpassed, perfect awakening." Master Cháng Bǎi: 如如 describes the many kinds of hardship a bodhisattva meets — countless.

quiz.q: "The more virtue grows, the more they conceal their goodness." What does each master cite?
options: Cháng Bǎi: Hánshān, Shídé, and Fēnggān hiding their virtue; Miào Jìng: the Analects, "unresentful when unrecognized"
quiz.why: "The more their virtuous qualities progressively increase, the more they conceal their own goodness, neither seeking that others know of it." Master Cháng Bǎi: if a bodhisattva lets people know his virtue, he passes away at once — like Hánshān, Shídé, and Chan Master Fēnggān of the Tang (tradition places them at Mount Tiāntāi). Venerable Miào Jìng: the Analects say, "is it not a joy to learn and practice … unresentful when others do not know you."

quiz.q: Bodhisattvas "train beings to become free of attachment." What skilful means does Master Cháng Bǎi describe?
options: giving one's own wealth for the stingy to give away, until they too become willing
quiz.why: "They remain free of attachment to their own body and wealth, and train other beings to become free of such attachment as well." Master Cháng Bǎi: the bodhisattva takes out his own wealth and asks such people to give it away; gradually they become willing to give — that's the bodhisattva's skill.

quiz.q: Towards the hostile, "performing acts that benefit and bring ease." How does Master Cháng Bǎi distinguish benefit and ease?
options: benefit aligns beings' thinking with the good; ease solves practical hardships
quiz.why: "Towards sentient beings who hold hostility against them, they constantly generate loving-kindness, and … perform every kind of act that genuinely benefits and brings ease." Master Cháng Bǎi: benefit means aligning beings' thinking with wholesome teachings; ease means solving practical difficulties of life.

quiz.q: "Not possessing a nature as language describes, yet not utterly nonexistent." How do the masters explain?
options: Cháng Bǎi: the snake isn't there, but the rope is; Miào Jìng: one part is absent, another remains — the ultimate nature
quiz.why: "Phenomena of this kind do not possess a nature exactly as language describes them, yet neither are they utterly nonexistent in every sense." Master Cháng Bǎi: the snake isn't there, but the rope still is. Venerable Miào Jìng: this part is absent; another part still exists — the ultimate nature of things.
